title: Al mercato, in treno
summary: Two small words Portuguese does not have: ne for quantities at the market, ci for places and travel times. Then buying a train ticket.
canDo: I can buy food at a market and say how much of it I want, using ne.
I can talk about places I go to with ci and say how long something takes.
I can buy a train ticket and understand platform, delay and changes.

items.back: Ne = "of it / of them". It stands in for a noun when you give a quantity: ne prendo due.
items.note: Quanti ne vuole? Ne prendo un chilo.
items.pt: Portuguese just drops the noun ("quero dois"). Italian cannot: it needs ne.

items.back: What can I get you? (literally "tell me", formal)

items.pt: PT pêssego. La pesca also means "fishing", as in Portuguese.

items.note: Un etto di prosciutto. Due etti = 200 grams.
items.pt: No everyday PT equivalent: Italians order cold cuts and cheese by the etto.

items.back: Ci = "there". It stands in for a place already mentioned: ci vado, ci sono stato.
items.pt: PT says "eu vou" or "vou lá". In Italian a bare "vado" sounds unfinished: say ci vado.

items.note: Sei mai stato a Roma? Non ci sono mai stato.
items.pt: Not PT "mais" (that is più). Mai = nunca / alguma vez.
PT plataforma. Italian stations number the tracks: binario 6.

items.note: Il treno è in ritardo di dieci minuti.

items.back: it takes (said of a train, a person)

lessons.title: Quanti ne vuole?
lessons.canDo: I can buy fruit and vegetables and say how much I want with ne.

intro.scene: Saturday morning at the market. Giulia stops at her usual fruit and vegetable stall.

lines.meaning: Good morning! What can I get you?
Good morning. I'd like some tomatoes.

lines.text: Ne prendo un chilo. E le pesche, quanto costano?
lines.meaning: I'll take a kilo. And the peaches, how much are they?

lines.text: Tre euro al chilo. Sono dolcissime.
lines.meaning: Three euros a kilo. They are really sweet.

lines.text: Allora ne prendo quattro. Basta così, grazie.
lines.meaning: Then I'll take four. That's all, thanks.

notes.title: Ne: "of them"
notes.body: When you give a quantity without repeating the noun, Italian puts ne before the verb: ne prendo un chilo, ne vorrei due, non ne voglio. The quantity can be a number, a weight, or a word like molti, pochi, un po'.

notes.title: Ne or lo, la, li, le?
notes.body: Le prendo = I'll take them (all of them). Ne prendo quattro = I'll take four of them. If there is a quantity, it is ne.

notes.title: 🇧🇷 PT tip: do not leave the gap
notes.body: Portuguese says "quero dois" and "não tenho". Italian needs the little word: ne voglio due, non ne ho. Also: dei pomodori, delle pesche, del pane = "some", where PT usually says nothing.

exercises.explain: With a number, use ne. "Le prendo" would mean all of them.

lessons.title: Ci vado ogni sabato
lessons.canDo: I can talk about places I go to with ci and say how long it takes to get there.

intro.scene: Marco and Leo are having coffee. Marco has a plan for tomorrow.

lines.text: Sei mai stato al mercato di Testaccio?
lines.meaning: Have you ever been to the Testaccio market?

lines.text: No, non ci sono mai stato. E tu?
lines.meaning: No, I've never been there. And you?

lines.text: Io ci vado ogni sabato. Ci vieni con me domani?
lines.meaning: I go there every Saturday. Will you come with me tomorrow?

lines.text: Volentieri! Quanto ci vuole da qui?
lines.meaning: Gladly! How long does it take from here?

lines.text: Ci vogliono venti minuti a piedi.
lines.meaning: It takes twenty minutes on foot.

notes.title: Ci: "there"
notes.body: Ci replaces a place you have already mentioned, and goes before the verb: ci vado, ci vieni?, non ci sono mai stato. Without it the sentence feels unfinished.

notes.title: Ci vuole, ci vogliono
notes.body: How long or how much something takes. The verb agrees with what follows: ci vuole un'ora, ci vogliono venti minuti, ci vogliono due uova.

notes.title: 🇧🇷 PT tip: three different ci
notes.body: Ci vado (there), ci vuole (it takes), ci vediamo (each other / us). Portuguese uses lá, leva and nos. In Italian it is always the same little word, so read the verb to know which one you have.

exercises.meaning: To the market? I go there every Saturday.
It takes twenty minutes from here.
exercises.explain: Venti minuti is plural, so vogliono.

exercises.prompt: "Sei mai stata a Napoli?" Sara has never been. She says:
options: No, non ci sono mai stata.

exercises.prompt: Listen. How long does it take?

options: We are going there at nine.

lessons.title: Un biglietto per Firenze
lessons.canDo: I can buy a train ticket and understand platform, delay and changes.

intro.scene: Roma Termini, the ticket office. Leo wants to spend Sunday in Florence.

lines.text: Buongiorno. Un biglietto per Firenze, per favore.
lines.meaning: Good morning. A ticket to Florence, please.

lines.text: Solo andata o andata e ritorno?
Andata e ritorno. A che ora parte il prossimo treno?
lines.meaning: Return. What time does the next train leave?

lines.text: Parte alle dieci e venti dal binario sei. Ma oggi è in ritardo di dieci minuti.
lines.meaning: It leaves at 10:20 from platform six. But today it is ten minutes late.

lines.text: No, è diretto. Ci mette un'ora e mezza. Si ricordi di convalidare il biglietto.
lines.meaning: No, it is direct. It takes an hour and a half. Remember to validate your ticket.

notes.title: Ci mette or ci vuole?
notes.body: Both say how long something takes. With metterci there is a subject doing the taking: il treno ci mette un'ora, io ci metto dieci minuti. With volerci there is not: ci vuole un'ora.

notes.title: At the station
notes.body: Dal binario sei = from platform six. In ritardo di dieci minuti = ten minutes late. In orario = on time. Diretto = no change; otherwise you hear "deve cambiare a Bologna".

notes.title: Convalidare
notes.body: Paper tickets for regional trains have to be stamped in the small machines on the platform before you get on. Tickets bought for a specific train, and digital tickets, usually do not.

exercises.text: Il treno ci ___ un'ora e mezza.
exercises.meaning: The train takes an hour and a half.
exercises.explain: The train is the subject, so metterci: il treno ci mette.

exercises.meaning: The train leaves from platform six.

options: Un biglietto di andata e ritorno.

options: The train is twenty minutes late

lessons.title: Lettura: Il sabato al mercato
lessons.canDo: I can read a short text about a routine and answer questions about it in Italian.

intro.scene: Giulia racconta il suo sabato mattina. Leggi, ascolta e poi rispondi.

sentences.text: Ogni sabato mattina vado al mercato del mio quartiere.
sentences.meaning: Every Saturday morning I go to the market in my neighbourhood.

sentences.text: Ci vado presto, perché dopo le dieci c'è troppa gente.
sentences.meaning: I go there early, because after ten there are too many people.

sentences.text: Compro sempre la frutta: adesso ci sono le pesche e ne prendo un chilo.
sentences.meaning: I always buy fruit: now there are peaches and I get a kilo.

sentences.text: Il mio venditore preferito si chiama Franco e lo conosco da dieci anni.
sentences.meaning: My favourite seller is called Franco and I have known him for ten years.

sentences.text: Franco mi consiglia sempre i pomodori migliori.
sentences.meaning: Franco always recommends the best tomatoes to me.

sentences.text: Ieri ne ho comprati due chili per fare il sugo.
sentences.meaning: Yesterday I bought two kilos of them to make sauce.

sentences.text: Il formaggio invece non lo compro al mercato: costa troppo.
sentences.meaning: Cheese, on the other hand, I don't buy at the market: it costs too much.

sentences.text: Dal mercato a casa mia ci vogliono solo cinque minuti a piedi.
sentences.meaning: From the market to my place it takes only five minutes on foot.

sentences.text: Torno a casa con le borse piene e sono contenta.
sentences.meaning: I go home with full bags and I am happy.

options: Perché il mercato chiude alle dieci.

exercises.prompt: Perché non compra il formaggio al mercato?
Quanto ci vuole dal mercato a casa sua?

meme.bottom: Came back with peaches, tomatoes and the full story of Franco's nephew

lessons.title: Racconto: Il treno sbagliato
lessons.canDo: I can follow a short spoken story about a journey and answer questions about it in Italian.

intro.scene: Leo racconta la sua domenica. Ascolta bene i numeri: binari, minuti, ore.

sentences.text: Domenica volevo andare a Firenze con Giulia.
sentences.meaning: On Sunday I wanted to go to Florence with Giulia.

sentences.text: Ho comprato due biglietti di andata e ritorno.
Il nostro treno partiva dal binario sei alle dieci e venti.
sentences.meaning: Our train was leaving from platform six at 10:20.

sentences.text: Ma io ho letto male e sono andato al binario sedici.
sentences.meaning: But I misread it and went to platform sixteen.

sentences.text: Sono salito sul treno e mi sono seduto. Giulia non c'era.
sentences.meaning: I got on the train and sat down. Giulia wasn't there.

sentences.text: Dopo dieci minuti è arrivato il controllore e ha guardato il mio biglietto.
sentences.meaning: After ten minutes the ticket inspector came and looked at my ticket.

sentences.text: Mi ha detto che quel treno andava a Napoli, non a Firenze.
sentences.meaning: He told me that train was going to Naples, not Florence.

sentences.text: Sono sceso alla prima stazione e ho aspettato un'ora.
sentences.meaning: I got off at the first station and waited an hour.

sentences.text: Sono arrivato a Firenze con due ore di ritardo.
sentences.meaning: I got to Florence two hours late.

sentences.text: Giulia mi aspettava in stazione. Rideva, ma non troppo.
sentences.meaning: Giulia was waiting for me at the station. She was laughing, but not too much.
